Consult Summary:
- Patient with acute mid-chest pressure and shortness of breath ongoing for several hours after gardening; risk factors include hypertension and hyperlipidemia; ambulance advised for urgent hospital evaluation to assess for cardiac etiology.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute chest discomfort described as mid-chest pressure (7/10), persistent; onset a few hours ago during gardening (digging in garden). Description: “someone sitting on my chest.”
- Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath, light-headedness, nausea (no vomiting); left shoulder/arm pain; calf pain with leg swelling.
- Symptom progression: Initially sudden onset; currently ongoing with similar severity.
- Exacerbating/initiating factors: Engaged in gardening at time of onset; previously relaxed just before onset.
- Relieving factors: None noted.
- Functional impact: Difficulties with climbing stairs and walking uphill; limits daily activity to moving around the house.
- Prior activity level: Generally able to garden every other week; typically fit and well aside from reported conditions.
- Past Medical History: Hypertension; hyperlipidemia.
- Medications: Do not take any medicines for HTN or hyperlipidemia.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Social History: Smokes tobacco; lives at home with wife; not further detailed.
- Family History: Not mentioned.
- Review of Systems: Breathing: shortness of breath; no detailed exam findings provided beyond this. Other systems not elaborated.

Past Medical History:
- Hypertension (high blood pressure)
- Hyperlipidemia (high cholesterol)

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected acute cardiac/or cardiovascular event (chest pressure with exertional SOB in patient with HTN and hyperlipidemia)
  - Plan:
    - Call ambulance for urgent transport to hospital for evaluation
    - Remain on the line to provide information to paramedics
    - Do not take any medications until evaluated
    - Stay calm; drink water if needed
    - Inform wife; gather belongings for hospital admission
    - In hospital: patient will be seen by a consultant immediately; paramedics will monitor chest and breathing and attach monitoring equipment (BP, heart rate) as part of assessment
    - The referring physician will be contacted with hospital updates; a follow-up appointment will be arranged after the hospital visit

- Issue 2: Shortness of breath with exertional limitation and leg symptoms (calf pain and leg swelling)
  - Plan:
    - Managed as part of urgent hospital evaluation for chest/breathing concerns
    - Hospital assessment by consultant including cardiovascular and respiratory evaluation

- Issue 3: Nausea
  - Plan:
    - Monitor; addressed during hospital evaluation as part of overall assessment

General Plan:
- Proceed with ambulance transport to hospital for urgent evaluation of potential cardiac etiology
- Hospital assessment by consultant with monitoring of chest/breathing; potential tests and treatments per hospital protocol
- Communication back to primary clinician; follow-up appointment to be scheduled after hospitalization
